newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool output to rise in '97/98-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool output to rise in '97/98-ABARE.

text.p: Australian wool production and prices are forecast to rise in 1997/98, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its March quarter Australian Commodities publication released on Tuesday.
Total production is forecast to rise by 1.2 percent to 690,000 tonnes while prices are forecast to rise by 8.3 percent to 650 cents a kg clean (Eastern market indicator), it said.
The rise in production, from a forecast 682,000 tonnes in 1996/97, is slightly less than the rise forecast by ABARE at its February Outlook conference, of 710,000 tonnes.
The forecast price rise is steady with the February forecast.

Wool prices were forecast to rise in 1997/98 in response to increased retail consumption in major wool consuming countries and anticipated lower sales from Wool International and grower stocks, ABARE said.
The final average price was estimated to have a 75 percent probability of being in the 575-695 cents a kg range, it said.
Demand for wool in 1997/98 is expected to increase mainly in response to higher economic growth in key wool consuming countries.
Stocks in processing pipelines are mostly at or below usual levels, ABARE said.

The rise in Australian wool production in 1997/98, with the shorn wool component forecast to increase to 645,000 tonnes, would be in response to small increases in both the number of sheep shorn and fleece weights, it said.
Australian exports in 1997/98 were expected to fall to 825,000 tonnes from 855,000 tonnes the year before, it said.
China was expected to remain the largest export destination for Australian wool but exports to China were not expected to increase significantly from the high levels of 1996/97, it said.
Wool production from the rest of the world was expected to remain flat at just less than one million tonnes clear in 1997/98, it said.
